taxonomy.label: Conditional boundary
taxonomy.literature_basis: Boundary comparisons such as < versus <= are recurrent novice logic mistakes.

taxonomy.label: Syntax and indentation
taxonomy.literature_basis: Beginner Python submissions frequently fail because of missing punctuation or block indentation.

taxonomy.label: Loop boundary and off-by-one
taxonomy.literature_basis: Loop bounds, termination conditions, and early return placement often cause wrong outputs.

taxonomy.label: Name and undefined variable
taxonomy.literature_basis: Variable-name mismatches and uninitialised local variables appear in real beginner submissions.

taxonomy.label: Type and operation misuse
taxonomy.literature_basis: Students may call methods incorrectly or use operations on incompatible values.

taxonomy.label: Input handling
taxonomy.literature_basis: Programs that assume missing or malformed input can fail even when their core algorithm is close.

taxonomy.label: List and indexing
taxonomy.literature_basis: Indexing and mutation during traversal can access elements outside a list or tuple.

taxonomy.label: Function return and call behaviour
taxonomy.literature_basis: Function tasks expose missing returns, printing instead of returning, and method-call confusion.

taxonomy.label: Algorithmic logic
taxonomy.literature_basis: Real submissions often run successfully but fail tests because the algorithmic state update is wrong.

taxonomy.label: Timeout and infinite loop
taxonomy.literature_basis: Non-terminating loops are an important sandbox and feedback boundary case for beginner programs.

taxonomy.label: Output formatting
taxonomy.literature_basis: Some novice submissions compute the right idea but fail exact-output tasks because of formatting.

taxonomy.label: Module import
taxonomy.literature_basis: Unavailable or misspelled imports should be identified as environment/import issues rather than logic bugs.
